verifications.claim: The final space shuttle launch was mission STS-135.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'The Space Shuttle program finished with its last mission, STS-135'; R2: 'STS-135 mission ... was the last space shuttle mission'; R3: 'the final space shuttle mission, STS-135'; R4: 'STS-135 is the final mission of NASA’s Space Shuttle Program'; R5: 'Last flight July 21, 2011 (STS-135)'
verifications.reasoning: All references explicitly identify STS-135 as the final mission.

verifications.claim: Mission STS-135 featured the orbiter Atlantis.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'STS-135 flown by Atlantis'; R2: 'Space Shuttle Atlantis' STS-135 mission'; R3: 'the last flight of the orbiter Atlantis'; R5: 'Atlantis's final flight'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state Atlantis flew STS-135.

verifications.claim: Atlantis lifted off from Kennedy Space Center in Florida on July 8, 2011, at 11:29 a.m. EDT.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'launched from Launch Pad 39A at Kennedy Space Center on July 8, 2011'; R3: 'lifted off from Launch Pad 39A at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center (KSC) in Florida on July 8, 2011'; R4: 'launching from NASA’s Kennedy Space Center at 11:29 a.m. EDT Friday' (July 8, 2011)
verifications.reasoning: Sources match date, time, location, and orbiter precisely.

verifications.claim: Mission STS-135 was commanded by Chris Ferguson.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Chris Ferguson commanded the mission'; R3: 'astronauts Christopher J. Ferguson'; R4: 'Space shuttle Commander Chris Ferguson'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm Ferguson as commander of STS-135.

verifications.claim: The crew of mission STS-135 included Pilot Doug Hurley, Mission Specialists Sandra Magnus, and Rex Walheim.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Doug Hurley was its pilot. Also aboard were Rex Walheim and Sandy Magnus'; R3: 'Douglas G. Hurley, Sandra H. Magnus, and Rex J. Walheim'; R4: 'Pilot Doug Hurley, Mission Specialists Sandy Magnus and Rex Walheim'
verifications.reasoning: Exact crew roles and names match across sources.

verifications.claim: Mission STS-135 launched from Launch Pad 39A, Kennedy Space Center.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'launched from Launch Pad 39A at Kennedy Space Center'; R3: 'lifted off from Launch Pad 39A at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center'
verifications.reasoning: Direct confirmation of launch pad and site.

verifications.claim: The objective of mission STS-135 was to deliver the Raffaello multi-purpose logistics module with over 8,000 pounds of supplies and spare parts to the International Space Station.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'carrying the Raffaello multipurpose logistics module and delivering supplies and spare parts to the International Space Station'; R3: 'delivered payloads and supplies to support the International Space Station'; R4: 'deliver the Raffaello multi-purpose logistics module filled with more than 8,000 pounds of supplies and spare parts to sustain space station operations'
verifications.reasoning: Precise match including module name, cargo weight, and destination.

verifications.claim: Mission STS-135 marked the end of NASA's 30-year space shuttle program.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Duration 1972–2011', 'first crewed flight April 12, 1981'; R3: 'brought an end to the 30-year space shuttle program'
verifications.reasoning: R3 directly states 30-year end; R1 supports timeline (1981-2011 ≈30 years).

verifications.claim: The Space Shuttle Program began with the first flight in April 1981.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'First crewed flight April 12, 1981 (STS-1)'; R5: 'First flight April 12, 1981 (STS-1)'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm first flight in April 1981 as program start.

verifications.claim: Atlantis landed back at Kennedy Space Center on July 21, 2011.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'landed at the KSC on July 21, 2011'; R3: 'night landing at KSC ... July 21'; R5: 'Last flight July 21, 2011 (STS-135)'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm Atlantis landing date and location.
